stem: How does the role of 'preventer' medication differ from 'reliever' medication in pediatric asthma management?

options.text: Preventers are long-term medications used daily, while relievers are for short-term symptom reversal
Preventers are only taken when the child is having an acute flare-up
Relievers should be taken every morning and night regardless of symptoms
Preventers are given in higher doses when the child is unwell

explanation: Preventers reduce airway inflammation over time to maintain control, whereas relievers quickly open the airways during symptomatic episodes.
rationale: One is for maintenance and long-term control, while the other is for 'rescue' or immediate symptom relief.

optionExplanations.A: Preventers reduce airway inflammation over time to maintain control, whereas relievers quickly open the airways during symptomatic episodes.
optionExplanations.B: Taking a preventer only during a flare is ineffective as these medications take time to build up and do not provide immediate relief.
optionExplanations.C: Relievers are generally used 'as needed' based on symptoms or before exercise, rather than as a scheduled maintenance therapy.
optionExplanations.D: In most pediatric cases, the preventer dose remains the same across all sections of the plan to maintain consistent baseline control.

source.hint: One is for maintenance and long-term control, while the other is for 'rescue' or immediate symptom relief.
